title: Months land on the same day; a missing day falls on month-end
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in as an Owner/Admin, or a user with "Settings Service" enabled, on the build under test. The Maintenance Reminders feature is on (it ships behind the maintenance_reminders flag).
  2. A schedule open in the editor with the service form ready. Seed it:
  3. ↳ Settings > Maintenance > New schedule (or open an existing schedule and Edit).
  4. ↳ Click Add service to open the blank service form.
  5. Prepare services to compare a months interval against a days interval, and a service completed on 31 January set to a 1-month interval.
custom_steps:
1. Set a service to a months interval and note the next due date after a completion.
  2. Set a service to a days interval and note how the date drifts.
  3. Complete a "1 month" service on 31 January and read the next due date, then the cycle after.
  4. Set up a service needed at two fixed points, and look for any one-time flag.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • A months interval resolves to the same day of a later month, counted from the last completion (a specific date, not a month); a days interval counts days and drifts against the calendar.
  • Where the anchor day does not exist in the target month, the date falls on that month's last day: 31 January + one month comes due 28 February, and the next cycle counts from 28 February.
  • A service needed at two fixed points is set up as two "At" rows; there is no one-time flag (a meter "At" row covers the one-off case).

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-3780; story SV-10559 (S2, Add a routine service to a schedule); Chunk 1 MR spec (Confluence 886931488), S2; read 29 Sep 2026. Source-verified 29 September 2026; not yet build-verified.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S2-R14: “A months interval resolves to the same day of a later month, counted from the last completion, and produces a specific date rather than a month. A days interval counts days and drifts relative to the calendar”
  • S2-E5: “Where the anchor day does not exist in the target month, the date falls on that month's last day. A service completed on 31 January and set to one month comes due 28 February, and the following cycle counts from that date”
  • S2-E2: “A service needed at two fixed points is set up as two At rows”
  • S2-E3: “There is no one-time flag. A meter At row covers the one-off case”
